title: Public API coverage
lead: Compare public SDK APIs with the app's settings, operations and visible results. The original inventory and denominator are retained. Each row distinguishes editable controls, fixed choices, code-only use and specific SDK input or platform limitations.
coverageGoal: The goal is to make supported SDK settings, operations, state queries and events accessible from the app. The current routes include typed values, collections, edited callbacks and actual SDK objects. Rows constrained by a getter-only declaration, SDK-owned lifecycle or unavailable platform consumer retain their individual explanation and original category.

Configuration APIs used combines individual GUI edits, fixed presets and code-only values. It is not the share of settings that users can edit. The tables calculate each percentage from the original API rows; an explanation does not remove an entry from that denominator.

The Web UI configuration inventory includes paths generated from Partial<ToggleSettingsPanelItem>, a component class rather than its constructor configuration type. These paths describe instance methods and event subscriptions. Supplying them as configuration does not call a method or subscribe to an event. Each affected row explains that input-contract mismatch.

Callback bodies need explicit execution permission, and object inputs use the corresponding factory or a current SDK instance. Fixed callback choices remain presets. Content, device and external-service requirements describe the conditions for executing a feature; they do not substitute for a GUI route. A documented no-op can still have a callable API and visible result.

API exposure and recorded execution results are measured separately. A subscription records a route for receiving an event; it does not show that every event occurred. Accepted settings and returned values also need feature-specific checks before they establish playback, remote-device behavior or service receipt.
